correctness.rationale: Fresh check of repairs/1/RESULT.md: for b=4a one has f(3/4)=−4a, and the next point in the lift is 5/4−4aμ. Writing c=cos(8πaμ), f there is 2a(1−c²)+4ac, so the normalized two-step displacement is exactly −2a(1−c)² at 3/4. This is negative for all sufficiently small nonzero μ, and the leading displacement is −a(8πa)^4 μ^5/2=−2048π⁴a⁵μ^5. At 0 the normalized displacement tends to 4a>0. Continuity gives a point satisfying F²(x)=x+1 for either sign. Integer equivariance proves F^(2k)(x)=x+k, hence real rotation 1/2. Half-translation conjugacy gives b=−4a; μ=0 is the half-turn itself. The repaired reproducibility note describes the unchanged finite diagnostic, not independent certification.
